name: issue_1066_door_close_restore_keeps_heat
description: Heat is armed on a cold mild-day morning (indoor 67F, floor 68F). A window opens (door/window pause) and closes again (restore). After the restore and at the next evaluation the thermostat must still be on heat. Before Issue #1066 the restore path re-armed the mild day's default edge (cool at the ceiling), putting the AC on a house that was below its comfort floor.
source: Issue #1066 plan, section on restore paths (door/window close, nat-vent exit, WHF stop, startup coalesce) re-arming a day-type default
notes: Occupant impact: closing a window must never turn the heating off and the AC on in a cold house.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: docs/08 section 6f 'Before / after' states that before #1066 restore paths 're-arm a day-type default without asking where indoor is'. On origin/main a mild day's default family is cooling, so the restore would re-arm cool at the ceiling and the hvac_mode_never_commanded(cool) and final comfort_family=heating assertions would fail; only a breach + deadband + sustain sequence could bring heat back. With nearest-edge arming the next evaluation (indoor 67 < 68) selects heat.
(b) Docs vs production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f 'Restore paths' paragraph and rule row 'indoor < floor -> heating'.
(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: after airing the room the occupant gets AC (or nothing) in a house that is already below its comfort floor.

Modeled in engine-only mode (tracker-driven sensor_open / sensor_close, the same events existing door/window goldens use). Coordinator debounce and state-listener timing is a track=integration concern and is not exercised here.
Classification fields: day_type=mild, hvac_mode=off, windows_recommended=true with 10:00/17:00 window times match classifier.py for DAY_TYPE_MILD.

events.note: Indoor 67F, 1F below the floor: heat armed (thermostat starts in heat).
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: Indoor 67F, 1F below the floor: heat armed (thermostat starts in heat).
Occupant opens a window: door/window pause takes over the HVAC (heat is saved as the pre-pause mode).
Window closed: pause ends, the pre-pause mode is restored.
Next scheduled evaluation after the restore: nearest-edge selector sees indoor 67 < floor 68 and keeps heat. Must not re-arm the mild day's default edge (cool).
Reactive reading after the evaluation: still heat.

assertions.reason: Across the whole pause/restore cycle the AC is never commanded: indoor is below the floor throughout, so the only correct armed edge is heat.
After the restore and the next evaluation the armed family is heating, not the mild day's default cooling.
The last commanded mode after the restore is heat.

verdict.summary: After a door/window pause and restore on a cold mild-day morning, the thermostat stays on heat and cool is never commanded.
verdict.observed_behavior: Pause at 07:00, restore at 07:10, evaluation at 07:15: heat remains the armed and last commanded mode.
verdict.expected_behavior: Restore paths no longer re-arm a day-type default; the nearest-edge selector picks the edge from indoor (docs/08 section 6f).
